sections.h2: Which Trigg County offices matter for a property tax bill?
sections.html:
Trigg County's tax offices are in Cadiz, the county seat, and the county clerk's website lists the phone numbers for all of them. The clerk's real estate department is at 38 Main Street and keeps hours of 8:00 am to 4:00 pm Monday through Friday.

  • Sheriff, (270) 522-6014: collects the current year's bills.
  • Property Valuation Administrator (PVA), (270) 522-3271: sets values, takes exemption applications and handles the conference that must come before any appeal.
  • County clerk, (270) 522-6661: handles recording, marriage licenses and delinquent taxes. Motor vehicle titles and renewals go through a separate line, (270) 522-0217.
  • County attorney, (270) 522-4733: mails the notices that come before a delinquent tax sale.

The clerk's office also closes for the Trigg County Ham Festival each October. In 2026 that meant half of Thursday, October 8 and all of Friday, October 9, so plan payoff requests around the festival week.

sections.h2: Why does Trigg County property differ from other Kentucky counties?
sections.html:
Trigg County is a lake county. It covers 481 square miles, 40 of them water, which is 8.3 percent of its area, and it sits on the far southwest edge of Kentucky beside Lake Barkley. Land Between the Lakes National Recreation Area, more than 170,000 acres with about 300 miles of natural shoreline on a peninsula between Kentucky Lake and Lake Barkley, reaches into the county. Cadiz is known as the Antique Capital of Western Kentucky, and Lake Barkley State Resort Park and Prizer Point Marina draw visitors to its shoreline.

The legislature formed the county in 1820 from parts of Christian and Caldwell counties and named it for Lt. Col. Stephen Trigg, killed at the Battle of Blue Licks in 1782. It borders Lyon, Caldwell, Christian, Calloway and Marshall counties in Kentucky and Stewart County, Tennessee. Cerulean (partly in Christian County) is a census-designated place, and Golden Pond is listed as a ghost town. The annual Trigg County Ham Festival each October is the best-known local event.

Population peaked at 14,539 in 1910, fell to 8,620 by 1970 and recovered to 14,061 in 2020. The Census Bureau estimates 14,512 for July 2025.

sections.h2: How many Trigg County homes are second homes or empty?
sections.html:
The Census numbers show a housing stock larger than the number of households. Trigg County has 7,733 housing units against 6,060 households, and the 2020 census counted 23.4 percent of housing units as vacant, the highest share among Spencer, Taylor, Todd and Trigg counties. The rental vacancy rate was 11.7 percent. A county built around two large lakes can show that pattern, though the Census does not give the reason.

  • Median owner-occupied home value is $207,700, and 76.9 percent of homes are owner-occupied.
  • Median gross rent is $803, and the median household income is $59,857.
  • Residents 65 or older make up 24.9 percent of the population, the largest senior share of the four counties, and the 2020 median age was 46.8.
  • The Census reported zero building permits for 2025.

With that many older owners, the homestead exemption is worth asking about early.

sections.h2: How do Trigg County tax bills and penalties work?
sections.html:
The bill is due on or before December 31 of the assessment year under the state's regular schedule. Pay in full by November 1 and you receive a 2 percent discount. From November 2 through December 31 you pay the face amount. A 5 percent penalty applies to January payments, and after January 31 it rises to 10 percent.

When the state delays the bills, the Department of Revenue can substitute an alternative schedule: due two full months after mailing, with the 2 percent discount for the first full month, the face amount for the next, a 5 percent penalty for one month after that, and 10 percent beyond. Bills open at the close of business on April 15 under the regular schedule transfer to the clerk as certificates of delinquency.

sections.h2: What was the 2026 Trigg County delinquent tax sale schedule?
sections.html:
The Trigg County Clerk runs one delinquent tax sale a year, held at the end of July in the year after taxes were due. The schedule for the 2025 bills, now in the past, shows how the process unfolds.

Trigg County 2026 delinquent tax sale for the 2025 bills (source: Trigg County Clerk)
StepDate
List of certificates published in the Cadiz RecordJune 4, 2026
Registration deadline for buyers, close of businessJuly 2, 2026
Tax sale at the clerk's office, 38 Main Street, 9:00 amJuly 17, 2026

The list could also be inspected at the clerk's office on weekdays from 8:00 am to 4:00 pm and on the clerk's website. Owners could pay at the clerk's office any time before the sale, and any payment that arrived after the sale was returned. Some advertised bills were excluded from the sale under KRS 134.504(10)(b). Each year's dates and rules document are posted on the clerk's delinquent tax page.

sections.h2: How can a Trigg County owner challenge an assessment?
sections.html:
The PVA values most homes by comparing recent sales of similar houses and must physically inspect each parcel at least once every four years. Contact the PVA first. State law requires a conference with the PVA or a deputy before an appeal, and it must happen before or during the inspection period. The roll is open to the public for thirteen days starting the first Monday of May. An owner who had that conference has until the next workday after the period ends to file with the county clerk.

The local board of assessment appeals convenes 25 to 35 days after the period closes and can sit up to five days. Bring evidence: physical details of the land and buildings, insurance policies, construction costs or listings of comparable property. Without documents, the board denies the appeal. Taxable personal property must be listed with the PVA between January 1 and May 15, and anything not listed by then counts as omitted.

sections.h2: Who qualifies for the Trigg County homestead exemption?
sections.html: The exemption is open to owners who are 65 or older or totally disabled and who own, occupy and maintain the home on January 1. For 2025 and 2026 it removes $49,100 from the assessed value. Applications go to the Trigg County PVA before December 31, and people classified as totally disabled by an agency outside Kentucky must renew yearly. Veterans with a service-connected total disability and people found totally and permanently disabled by Social Security file once.

sections.h2: What should I do about taxes when selling a Trigg County house?
sections.html: Ask the sheriff for the current payoff and the clerk for any certificate of delinquency. Kentucky treats each year's tax as the personal debt of whoever owned the parcel on January 1, and a delinquent lien follows the property for as long as eleven years whoever owns it. If a purchaser at the July sale holds the certificate, the payoff goes to that purchaser.

faqs.q: Who collects property tax in Trigg County?
faqs.a: The sheriff collects current bills, and you can call (270) 522-6014. After April 15 unpaid bills move to the county clerk at (270) 522-6661.

faqs.q: When is the Trigg County delinquent tax sale held?
faqs.a: It is held once a year at the end of July. The 2026 sale took place on July 17, 2026, at 9:00 am in the clerk's office, and the next one will be listed on the clerk's delinquent tax page.

faqs.q: Can I still pay once my Trigg County bill is advertised?
faqs.a: Yes, until the sale. The clerk accepts delinquent payments at 38 Main Street before the sale date, and payments received after the sale are returned.

faqs.q: How much is the homestead exemption in Trigg County?
faqs.a: It is $49,100 for 2025 and 2026. File with the Trigg County PVA at (270) 522-3271 before December 31 if you are 65 or older or totally disabled.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Trigg County house that owes back taxes?
faqs.a: Yes, because the tax is paid from the proceeds at closing. Get payoff figures from the sheriff and the clerk first so the buyer's closing agent can clear the lien.
